title: Multiplicativity of regularized determinants
statement: For specified admissible elliptic operators and a fixed regularization, determine the defect \(\log\det(AB)-\log\det A-\log\det B\), and conditions under which it vanishes. The operator order, spectral cuts, commutativity, and treatment of kernels must be fixed.
status: As of 12 November 2026, the multiplicative anomaly and its local-residue description are established in the settings treated by \citet{kontsevichvishik1994geometry}. Unqualified multiplicativity is false; this occurrence reuses the earlier precise problem.

title: Odd-moduli integration and the higher-genus RNS measure
statement: For super Riemann surfaces of a fixed genus and spin parity, determine the odd-moduli pushforward of the RNS measure on any specified projection domain, its modular transformation, and its degeneration behavior. Separately determine whether a global holomorphic projection to reduced spin moduli exists.
status: As of 12 November 2026, the global-projection premise is obstructed for \(g\geq5\) by Donagi--Witten and for both parity components in every \(g\geq3\) by the theorem stated in the September 2026 Correa--Donagi--Noja preprint. Local odd integration remains meaningful. The 2025 genus-three analysis proves a three-term form but leaves its exact coefficient values conjectural and its numerical extraction without a rigorous error bound. Thus that coefficient determination remains a precise partial remainder; no general unsolved global projection is asserted.

title: Which lattice theta sums have the required modular transformation?
statement: For a positive-definite lattice, determine the modular transformation of its theta series, specifying the modular group and scalar, multiplier, or vector-valued representation. The seminar asks whether the desired full-group scalar transformation forces even unimodularity.
status: As of 12 November 2026, Poisson summation gives the precise dual-lattice transformation, and even unimodular lattices supply the full modular-group scalar form in the stated convention. Theta series of other integral lattices remain modular for suitable subgroups or vector-valued representations, so the unrestricted only-if assertion is false. This is a settled clarification, not a new open problem.

title: A common linear complex structure for real codimension-two arrangements
statement: Given real codimension-two linear subspaces \(L_i\subset\mathbb R^{2m}\), decide whether there is a real linear operator \(J\) with \(J^2=-I\) and \(J(L_i)=L_i\) for every \(i\). A 2-arrangement also imposes even-codimension intersection conditions; these are additional hypotheses, not an automatic consequence of the individual codimensions.
status: As of 12 November 2026, the proposed automatic complexification is false. For pairwise transverse planes in \(\mathbb R^4\), \citet[Theorems 1 and 3]{batzies2007planes} gives simultaneous-conjugacy and four-plane criteria. The chapter rederives a bounded linear-algebra formulation as an annotation to known work, with no new research claim and no inference that a higher-dimensional classification is an open problem. Topological equivalence is not settled by the linear criterion.

title: Polynomial quotients of the affine type-A Hecke algebra
statement: For \(q\ne0\), identify the universal quotient of the affine type-A Hecke algebra by \(p(X_n)=0\), where \(p\) is monic of degree \(r\) with nonzero constant term, and determine its dimension and a basis; the notebook singles out \(p(z)=z^2-1\).
status: As of 12 November 2026, this is the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type \(G(r,1,n)\), of dimension \(r^n n!\); \(r=2\) yields type B. The Ariki--Koike basis theorem holds without semisimplicity, as read in \citet[\S2, (2.2)]{mathas2004matrix}. The universal quotient target answers the precise notebook reading adopted here; it is not a claim of an evaluation into the original finite type-A algebra for every polynomial.

title: Faithfulness of universal Burau representations
statement: Determine the ranks \(n\) for which the Burau representation over \(\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]\) is faithful.
status: As of 12 November 2026, faithful for \(n\le3\), unfaithful for \(n\ge5\). A July 2026 preprint, revised September 2026, claims faithfulness for \(n=4\); its main theorem was read but not independently checked here.

title: Three- and four-dimensional reduced planar gauge models
statement: For a specified one-site unitary plaquette model, determine its nonperturbative planar free energy and Wilson loops, with the center-symmetry conditions needed for volume reduction made explicit.
status: As of 12 November 2026 the general all-coupling planar solution is unavailable in the sources checked; exact two-dimensional reductions and higher-dimensional numerical methods are established. Unconditional equivalence of the original untwisted model with four-dimensional weak-coupling gauge theory is false.

title: Commuting quantizations of local KdV Hamiltonians
statement: Construct commuting normally ordered deformations of the complete family of classical local KdV integrals.
status: As of 12 November 2026 solved as an algebraic/formal and generic-parameter construction; spectral classification and exceptional representation specializations are distinct questions.

title: Quantum KdV spectrum in irreducible Virasoro representations
statement: For fixed central charge and highest weight, determine the joint spectral and Jordan data of the commuting quantum KdV charges on the irreducible highest-weight module.
status: As of 12 November 2026 partly solved, with explicit constructions and special-regime results. The opened 2026 Masoero--Ruzza v1 proves a particular c=-2 admissible-QQ completeness statement for nonintegral momentum; it is not an arbitrary-parameter theorem. The chapter provides a checked level-two Jordan obstruction in a nonunitary irreducible quotient.

title: Quantization of second Adler--Gelfand--Dickey structures
statement: Construct a quantum algebra deforming the second Gelfand--Dickey bracket on monic scalar operators of arbitrary order, in the principal Drinfeld--Sokolov setting.
status: As of 12 November 2026 the quantum W-algebra/BRST construction resolves the algebraic problem, with precise generic-parameter identifications in the cited sources.

title: Finite equational basis for subspace-lattice identities
statement: Do identities valid in subspace lattices of all finite-dimensional rational vector spaces follow from finitely many lattice identities? This is the explicit equational reading of the notebook question about linear equivalence.
status: As of 12 November 2026 the stated rational formulation and the analogous all-field variety have a negative answer by Herrmann (1984), Theorem 1.4. The field and type of axioms were not stated in the notebook; the decidability problem GP-1985-20 is different.

title: Preprojective reduction of the free modular lattice
statement: Describe the quotient of \(D^r\) by equality in all indecomposable preprojective rational representations and characterize its represented subspace families.
status: As of 12 November 2026 the 1987 Gelfand--Lidskii--Ponomarev theorem gives a precise large-rank answer through compatible eventually generated families and graded right ideals. The present chapter uses the safely verified subrange r>=7; it does not turn the historical r=5 exception into a present-day open claim.

title: The two-source unitary orbital integral
statement: Evaluate \(\int_{U(N)}\exp\sum_{\mu=1}^2\operatorname{Tr}(U^*P_\mu UQ_\mu)\,dU\) for diagonal source matrices, specifying whether the target is a convergent series, a compact finite formula or large-\(N\) information.
status: As of 12 November 2026, the general integral has exact convergent Haar expansions; an explicit rank-two formula and rank-three expansions appear in \citet{holguin2024multimatrix}. The chapter develops a checked finite-rank formula and controlled series. No general compact HCIZ-type determinant or general large-\(N\) solution is claimed.

title: Riemann hypothesis in the toroidal and horocycle formulations
statement: Do all nontrivial zeros of \(\zeta(s)\) satisfy \(\operatorname{Re}s=1/2\)? In the recorded approach, can toroidal spectral parameters be put in a suitable positive unitary realization, or equivalently can the requisite RH-strength horocycle remainders be proved under the stated test-function hypotheses?
status: Open as of 12 November 2026. The toroidal structure theorems and qualitative horocycle equidistribution are established, but the positivity and zero-location conclusions are not.

title: Orientable gluings of a labelled polygon by genus
statement: For a labelled oriented \(2n\)-gon, count orientation-reversing pairings of its sides whose quotient has genus \(g\), with cyclic rotations kept distinct.
status: Solved before the recorded discussions by Harer and Zagier (1986), with an exact coefficient formula, a recurrence, and a Gaussian-matrix derivation. As of 12 November 2026 this is an established enumeration theorem.

title: Coloured planar maps with controlled face counts and interfaces
statement: Enumerate rooted orientable planar maps with specified numbers of faces of the prescribed degrees and colours, and a specified number of edges between unlike colours; specify primal/dual and rooting conventions before extracting coefficients.
status: As of 12 November 2026, formal multi-matrix generating functions and the planar Ising solution provide the recorded framework. The notebook does not select a unique finer counting convention, so no unsolved numerical problem is inferred.

title: Artin holomorphy for nontrivial irreducible complex representations
statement: For every nontrivial irreducible continuous finite-dimensional complex representation \(\rho\) of the absolute Galois group of a number field, is its Artin L-function entire?
status: Open in general as of 12 November 2026; Brauer induction proves meromorphic continuation, and abelian, monomial and numerous other cases are known. Recent partial holomorphy criteria do not establish the universal conjecture.

title: The normalized mean-field spin-glass ground energy
statement: Determine the deterministic limit of \(N^{-1}\min_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^N}N^{-1/2}\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j\) for independent standard Gaussian couplings.
status: Solved in the variational sense as of 12 November 2026 by the zero-temperature Parisi formula of Auffinger and Chen (2016 preprint; 2017 publication). This is a mean-field theorem, with the normalization and Gaussian assumptions explicit.

title: Parisi ultrametricity of asymptotic spin-glass overlaps
statement: Identify a rigorous thermodynamic interpretation of the hierarchical overlap assertion and prove ultrametricity of the resulting replica array.
status: As of 12 November 2026, Panchenko\textquoteright s theorem proves ultrametricity for random overlap measures satisfying the Ghirlanda--Guerra identities (2011 preprint; 2013 publication). It does not assert ultrametricity for arbitrary finite near-ground-state sets.

title: Explicit integral and de Rham comparison for Chern classes
statement: Construct explicit Cech/de Rham comparison data, preferably through low-weight motivic complexes, for the integral Chern classes of a holomorphic vector bundle.
status: As of 12 November 2026, functorial Deligne Chern classes exist, and inspected explicit weight-two formulas construct the comparison through the Bloch complex and dilogarithm. The announced 1987 paper is bibliographically identified, but its complete higher-weight formulas were not inspected. This access limitation is not classified as mathematical openness.

title: Beilinson--Soule motivic vanishing
statement: For every field \(F\), positive weight \(p\), and \(j\le0\), prove \(H^j(F,\mathbb Q(p))=0\); compare with the stronger integral sheaf-amplitude requirement \([1,p]\) stated in the notebook.
status: Open in general as of 12 November 2026. Modern motivic complexes exist, the upper-degree comparison with Milnor K-theory is established, and important arithmetic cases are known. Garkusha\textquoteright s criteria and Soul\'e\textquoteright s 4 November 2026 interview explicitly retain the general lower-degree conjecture.
